args.goal: Resolve the existing Ghost diagnostic's unexecuted upstream dependency using public package artifacts and installed offline tools. Check equivalent evidence and claim actual ownership first. Read products/sites/ghost-import-diagnostic/package/README.md, package.json, harness.cjs, fixtures.json and relevant saved lessons. Check the exact metadata FETCH receipt before reading its artifact. Establish the actual dependency closure, supported runtime and artifact sizes before substantial preparation. Use only official registry metadata and its exact linked package artifacts; no guessed endpoints, npm network access through EXEC, credentials, spending or installations outside the isolated job. Limit discovery to ten package-version metadata records and stop if a complete runnable closure cannot fit that bound or response limits. Do not substitute stubs or reimplement the converter. If feasible, execute the unchanged harness against actual pinned upstream code in an isolated offline job, recording exact versions, hashes, commands, exit codes and per-case observations. Treat downloaded code as untrusted; do not execute lifecycle scripts. Save only minimal results and dependency provenance under products/services/ghost-upstream-execution/, respecting redistribution terms. If infeasible, save the specific demonstrated prerequisite and reconsideration trigger; do not repeat capability discovery or generate another prototype. Distinguish converter execution from real Ghost import, customer delivery and revenue. No public edits, deployment, submissions, outreach, accounts or agreements. Read saved results before completing with an actual valid lease and a lesson. Preserve every existing observation and retirement obligation; later public changes require exact-digest independent review.

description: Five unclassified feedback sources leave demand unknown; no funding or revenue is verified. The existing Ghost diagnostic has only stub execution evidence.
